mechanics.summary: One fast driving action safely moves a vehicle its on-road or off-road combat-speed rating in 10-meter hexes.

outcome.value: move listed on-road or off-road combat speed in 10-meter hexes

exceptions: Only pavement hexes count as on-road.

unknowns: Road status requires scene data.

mechanics.summary: Immediately after safe movement, a successful terrain-modified DRIVING roll moves the vehicle an additional number of hexes equal to combat speed plus one per success beyond the first.
trigger: driver attempts movement beyond safe distance
inputs: terrain of vehicle hex after safe movement

outcome.value: combat speed plus one hex per success after first

exceptions: A failed roll leaves the vehicle stuck after safe movement.

unknowns: Terrain modifier and rolled successes require data.

mechanics.summary: Failure on the extra-movement DRIVING roll leaves the vehicle stuck after it has moved its safe distance.

outcome.value: vehicle becomes stuck after safe movement

mechanics.summary: A stuck vehicle can be freed with a terrain-modified DRIVING roll as a slow action; failure makes it bogged down.

unknowns: Terrain modifier requires scene data.

mechanics.summary: A bogged-down vehicle requires occupants to get out and make a STAMINA roll taking one stretch to move it; helpers may assist, and another vehicle at least as large gives +2.
exceptions: The +2 applies only when the other vehicle is at least as large as the bogged-down vehicle.

unknowns: Vehicle relative size and helper eligibility require input.

mechanics.summary: At the end of a movement action, the driver may face the vehicle toward any hex side; facing cannot be changed at another time.

outcome.value: set facing to a hex side

exceptions: Changing facing is not an action itself.

mechanics.summary: Each bane rolled after pushing a DRIVING roll reduces vehicle reliability by 1; at zero the vehicle breaks down and becomes inoperable before extra movement.

value.zero: break down and become inoperable before extra movement

mechanics.summary: Firing a vehicle smoke launcher is a slow action requiring no roll and fills every hex adjacent to the vehicle with dense smoke.

value.smoke: dense smoke in all adjacent hexes

mechanics.summary: Small-arms attacks against vehicles receive +2 for target size.
exceptions: Heavy weapons do not receive this modifier; it does not apply to bicycles or motorcycles.

mechanics.summary: Firing any hand-held or mounted weapon from a vehicle gives -2 if the vehicle moved since the shooter's previous turn.
trigger: vehicle-mounted or hand-held weapon fired from vehicle
vehicle moved since shooter's previous turn
exceptions: Stabilizers negate this modifier.

unknowns: Movement since the previous turn needs combat history.

mechanics.summary: An attack against a vehicle receives -1 if the target vehicle moved since the shooter's previous turn.
trigger: target vehicle moved since shooter's previous turn

unknowns: Movement since the previous turn needs combat history.

mechanics.summary: Use the vehicle's front, side, or rear armor facing the attacker, modified by the weapon armor modifier, to reduce vehicle damage.

outcome.value: damage reduced by modified directional armor

exceptions: Top and bottom attacks use rear armor.

unknowns: Attack angle requires token positions and facing.

mechanics.summary: An attack is fully deflected if its base weapon damage is two steps or more lower than the modified vehicle armor level, regardless of rolled attack successes.
After vehicle armor is penetrated, roll a D6; on a bane, reduce its armor level by 1. A TECH roll after one shift restores one armor level per success up to original rating.

value.repair: +1 armor per success, capped at original

mechanics.summary: A vehicle hit rolls D10 on the penetration or no-penetration component-damage column. Penetrating hits reduce damage by armor first; non-penetrating hits apply full damage.
exceptions: For penetrating hits, reroute a missing or destroyed result upward toward #1 to a present component. For non-penetrating hits, a missing or destroyed result has no effect. Re-roll track/wheel for front and rear attacks.

unknowns: Present components and occupant assignment require vehicle state.

mechanics.summary: For a penetrating hit, damage exceeding that needed to destroy or incapacitate a component continues upward through present components, except that engine excess damage stops; non-penetrating hits never cause secondary damage.
trigger: penetrating component hit has excess damage

outcome.value: apply remaining damage to next present higher table row

exceptions: Engine stops excess damage.
Non-penetrating hits do not cause secondary damage.

unknowns: Component capacities and presence require data.

mechanics.summary: Fuel damage of 1 or more halves maximum fuel capacity and immediately loses fuel above that capacity; explosive damage with at least one blast success ignites Intensity-C fire, forces occupant CUF rolls, lasts one stretch, and destroys the vehicle beyond repair.

value.explosiveBlastSuccess: Intensity C fire; occupants CUF; vehicle destroyed after one stretch

unknowns: Explosion successes and occupants require context.

mechanics.summary: Each engine, suspension, radio, or mounted-weapon damage point reduces that component's reliability by 1; at zero it is inoperable and must be repaired.
trigger: engine, suspension, radio, or mounted weapon component takes damage

outcome.value: reliability -1 per damage; zero is inoperable

exceptions: Engine excess damage stops; suspension and radio excess damage continues. A typical radio has reliability 1.

mechanics.summary: One ammunition damage destroys half stored ammunition and two destroys all. Heavy-weapon ammunition has a 50% D6 4+ explosion risk at one damage and automatically explodes at two; an explosion increases ammunition blast power one step to maximum A and destroys the vehicle beyond repair.
exceptions: Excess damage continues to another component.

unknowns: Ammunition type, blast, and quantity require vehicle inventory data.

mechanics.summary: Cargo or external-stores results damage a random stored item. Driver, passenger, gunner, commander, and exposed-passenger results resolve normal attack damage, hit location, and critical injury against the selected occupant; driver replacement is a fast action.
trigger: component table selects cargo, external stores, or occupant
exceptions: Passenger, gunner, and commander excess damage continues; exposed passenger is outside or partly outside vehicle.

unknowns: Random selection and occupant positions require data.

mechanics.summary: Tracks or wheels can be hit only from the side. Damage above half side armor, rounded up and then modified by weapon armor modifier, reduces vehicle reliability by 1 per qualifying damage point; otherwise it has no effect.
trigger: track or wheel component is hit

outcome.value: reliability -1 per damage point above modified ceil(side armor / 2)

exceptions: At reliability zero, vehicle is inoperable and must be repaired.

unknowns: Attack side requires facing data.

mechanics.summary: One or more damage to a fire-control system makes it inoperable; one or more damage to an antenna makes the vehicle radio inoperable. Both require repair.
trigger: fire-control system or antenna takes at least one damage

mechanics.summary: A ricochet result requires every exposed person outside the vehicle or on foot in the same hex to make an immediate CUF roll.

outcome.value: immediate CUF roll for each exposed person

unknowns: Exposure state requires input.

mechanics.summary: When an explosive weapon penetrates a vehicle, every occupant suffers the explosion in addition to direct damage; vehicle armor does not reduce blast power.

outcome.value: apply full blast power to all occupants

unknowns: Occupant list requires vehicle state.

mechanics.summary: Every occupant of a penetrated vehicle makes an immediate CUF roll; failure requires immediate bail-out on their next turn by spending a slow action, replacing normal CUF effects.
exceptions: This replaces normal CUF-roll effects.

mechanics.summary: Turret weapons do not expose gunner; coaxial weapons also cannot fire in the same round as main weapon; hull mounts fire only in their listed direction; pintles expose arms and head, though a gun shield protects arms only.

value.coaxial: gunner not exposed; cannot fire same round as main weapon
value.hull: gunner not exposed; listed firing direction only
value.pintle: arms and head exposed; gun shield protects arms only

unknowns: Gunner exposure and firing direction require vehicle state.

mechanics.summary: A secondary vehicle weapon may be fired by crew who are not performing another task; passengers may take over a pintle-mounted weapon when no dedicated gunner is available.
trigger: vehicle secondary or pintle weapon is fired

outcome.value: eligible crew fires secondary weapon; passenger may take uncrewed pintle

unknowns: Current crew tasks and dedicated-gunner availability require input.

mechanics.summary: A mounted weapon loses 1 reliability per damage and becomes inoperable at zero; for armored tank guns and similar vehicle weapons, damage is first reduced by half the vehicle front armor, rounded up and modified by weapon armor modifier.
trigger: mounted vehicle weapon component takes damage

outcome.value: for armored mounted weapon, reduce damage by modified ceil(front armor / 2); then reliability -1 per damage

unknowns: Whether a specific mounted weapon is armored requires item data.

mechanics.summary: A stabilizer removes the -2 modifier for firing while moving.
trigger: stabilized vehicle weapon fires from moving vehicle

mechanics.summary: Advanced fire control removes moving-fire penalties and all range modifiers: attacks with the system through EXTREME range resolve as SHORT range.
trigger: vehicle weapon with advanced fire control attacks at range through Extreme

mechanics.summary: Aimed fire at a listed external vehicle component takes -2, is offset by the +2 small-arms vehicle modifier, can target tracks or wheels only from the side, and never penetrates armor.
trigger: attacker calls shot against external vehicle component
exceptions: Small-arms called shot modifier is offset by the small-arms vehicle modifier.
Called shots never penetrate armor.

unknowns: Called component is player input.

mechanics.summary: After a shift scavenging a functional or inoperable vehicle, a TECH roll yields vehicle spare parts equal to successes. A permanently destroyed vehicle yields one fewer part and is permanently destroyed by scavenging, so cannot be scavenged again.
trigger: actor scavenges vehicle for one shift

value.permanentlyDestroyed: successes minus one; vehicle cannot be scavenged again

unknowns: Vehicle state and scavenge completion require tracking.

mechanics.summary: Ramming is a fast action against a same-hex target, using opposed DRIVING; an individual target rolls MOBILITY instead, and only the attacker spends an action. On a hit, damage equals rear armor plus one per attacker success beyond the first.

outcome.value: rear armor plus one damage per success after first

mechanics.summary: On vehicle ramming, the attacker takes unmodified damage equal to the target's rear armor; target damage strikes the facing side, while attacker damage strikes its front.

outcome.value: apply target rear armor damage to attacker front and ram damage to target attacked side

mechanics.summary: A ramming attack against an individual has critical threshold 2 and causes no damage to the attacking vehicle.
A horse typically has combat speed 2 on-road and off-road; mounted movement may be doubled using MOBILITY instead of DRIVING.

unknowns: Specific horse combat speed can differ from typical value.

mechanics.summary: Shooting from horseback is -2 with a one-handed firearm or -3 with a two-handed firearm. Mounted close combat requires one-handed weapon; attacks against rider take -1, and attacker selects rider or horse as target.
trigger: attack is made from or against horseback
exceptions: Rider specialty negates horseback shooting modifiers.

unknowns: Weapon handedness and target selection require data or input.

mechanics.summary: A hit mount makes no CUF roll; rider immediately rolls MOBILITY or is thrown, taking 1 damage. Typical horse capacity is 5, heals 1 damage per shift, needs Medical Aid within a shift when incapacitated or is put down, and any horse critical injury is immediately fatal.

value.incapacitation: Medical Aid within shift or put down

mechanics.summary: For boats, a penetrating suspension hit of one or more damage breaches the hull and starts sinking; at each round start roll D6, and a bane sinks and loses the boat.
trigger: boat suspension takes one or more penetrating damage

value.eachRound: D6 bane sinks and loses boat

mechanics.summary: Each passenger uses 25 cargo units; a trailer can carry up to the vehicle cargo value, doubling capacity, but halves combat and travel speeds.
trigger: vehicle cargo capacity or speed is calculated
exceptions: Crew do not use cargo capacity.

mechanics.summary: Vehicles marked as amphibious by preparation require one stretch of preparation; afterward they move through shallow water and swamp unhindered. The BMD-2 is amphibious without preparation.
trigger: marked vehicle prepares for amphibious movement

outcome.value: move through shallow water and swamp unhindered

exceptions: BMD-2 needs no preparation.

unknowns: Which vehicle variants carry the printed amphibious marker requires reference data.

values.combatSpeed: 10-m hexes per combat driving action, on-road/off-road plus W/T mode

referenceData.notes: Individual vehicle-list rows are static profiles for the reference-tables-and-derived-values batch.
Mount-code effects are extracted in vehicle.combat.weapon-mounts and vehicle combat weapon records.
Operational entries are preserved in vehicle.combat.component.table.
